newsitem.title: CANADA: Hollinger ups Southam debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Hollinger ups Southam debt deal.

text.p: Hollinger Inc said on Tuesday that it sweetened its offer to holders of its 7 percent Southam Inc-linked convertible debentures as part of its deal to acquire the rest of the newspaper chain.

Hollinger originally offered C$23.50 a share in cash and a special share to acquire the Southam stock it did not already own. Last week it raised the estimated value of the offer to C$23.55 to C$23.95 a share.
Some minority shareholders had been unhappy with the original offer.

Hollinger said debt holders could now choose to receive compensation similar to Southam shareholders. For each $1,000 of debentures, holders could choose to be paid $771.43 in cash and $571.43 in special convertible shares, Hollinger said.
Hollinger first proposed an all-cash, early conversion of the debentures on April 30.
Debenture holders could receive the conversion value in cash alone as long as the special share alternative was available, Hollinger said.
